codeQuality.summary: The code has several critical issues including a clear bug on line 7 (no-op if statement), lack of database initialization checks that will cause runtime errors, and heavy use of 'any' types that eliminate TypeScript's safety benefits. Security is reasonable with parameterized queries, but maintainability suffers from inconsistent error handling, missing type definitions, and global mutable state. Recommend: fix line 7 bug immediately, add initialization guards, create proper TypeScript interfaces, and standardize error handling patterns.

testCoverage.summary: The src/db.ts file has zero test coverage. All six exported functions are completely untested. Critical gaps include: no validation of database initialization, no edge case handling for invalid IDs or empty text, inconsistent error handling (some functions swallow errors, others re-throw), a bug in initDb() where the early return is broken (line 7), and no tests for the soft-delete pattern or migration execution. The code needs comprehensive unit tests covering happy paths, error conditions, edge cases like non-existent IDs, empty strings, and proper database state management.

recommendations.description: Fix the critical bug on line 7 of src/db.ts where 'if(db) db;' is a no-op statement. This should be 'if(db) return;' to prevent re-initialization of the database. This bug will cause the database to be reinitialized on every call to initDb(), potentially causing data corruption or migration errors.

The entire codebase has 0% test coverage. All six exported functions (initDb, addTodo, getTodos, toggleTodo, updateTodo, deleteTodo) are completely untested. Create comprehensive unit tests covering happy paths, error conditions, edge cases (non-existent IDs, empty strings), database initialization, and migration execution before deploying to production.

Five functions (addTodo, getTodos, toggleTodo, updateTodo, deleteTodo) lack null/initialization checks for the 'db' variable. If any of these functions are called before initDb(), they will throw 'Cannot read property of null' errors. Add initialization guards at the start of each function or refactor to a class-based pattern with proper state management.

The file uses 'any' type extensively (db variable, migration callbacks), bypassing TypeScript's type safety. Define proper interfaces for NeverChangeDB and migration types, or create type definitions for the 'neverchange' package to restore type checking and prevent runtime errors.

Error handling is inconsistent across functions. addTodo() swallows errors without re-throwing, getTodos() and toggleTodo() have no error handling at all, while updateTodo() and deleteTodo() properly catch and re-throw. Standardize error handling to ensure all database errors are properly logged and propagated to callers.

None of the CRUD functions validate their inputs. Functions accept empty strings, non-existent IDs, and don't verify that operations actually affected any rows. Add validation for text parameters (non-empty, reasonable length) and ID existence checks to prevent silent failures.

Global mutable state (module-level 'db' variable) makes the code difficult to test and can lead to race conditions. Refactor to a class-based pattern (TodoDatabase class) with proper dependency injection, initialization guards, and support for multiple instances if needed. This improves testability and maintainability.

Extract migrations and SQL queries to named constants for better maintainability. This makes it easier to review all database schema changes and queries in one place, prevents typos through reuse, and improves code organization by separating data from logic.

Add JSDoc comments to all exported functions documenting parameters, return types, thrown errors, and behavior. Replace console.log statements with a proper logging framework or environment-based logging to avoid cluttering production logs with debug messages.

Minor formatting inconsistencies exist throughout the file (inconsistent spacing in array parameters, closing brackets on different lines). Apply consistent formatting using a tool like Prettier to improve code readability.
